posts.text:
What can Europe do to address aggressive actions by Russia in space?

Aleix Nadal Campos of @RANDEurope discusses: bit.ly/4m4jhyS

Any AGI strategy, whether it favors acceleration or caution, "must demonstrate that it preserves a sufficient level of human agency and choice to, at minimum, allow course correction."

New paper: bit.ly/482IR1u

"There's a lot of interest right now in housing affordability, a lot of momentum for policy changes. Our main priority is to make the most of this opening to produce some helpful, credible, and timely research." bit.ly/4tla8EM

"To the extent that the operation [in Iran] has struggled, it's not because the United States lacks options," says RAND's Raphael Cohen. "Rather, it's because each pathway comes with trade-offs." bit.ly/4bZnOzv

Growing numbers of U.S. students from middle school through college report using AI to help with homework.

Yet many of these same students express concerns about how using AI for schoolwork might harm their critical thinking skills. bit.ly/4cNDhTZ

The war in Iran is not the catastrophe that some make it out to be, says RAND's Raphael Cohen.

"The war has already succeeded in setting the Iranian threat back, and the United States retains multiple pathways forward." bit.ly/3O3NYHR
New report: Teacher turnover in urban school districts remains elevated compared with suburban and rural districts. bit.ly/4sxxffi

Russian satellites have shadowed the same European spacecraft for months, sometimes approaching within five kilometers of their targets.

This does not fit the profile of simple surveillance, says RAND Europe’s Aleix Nadal Campos. bit.ly/4dr7R65

In a world with AGI, humanity must preserve its survival, capacity for agency, and strategic optionality.

That will require an ecosystem where humans and AI coexist while retaining human agency—and a global security architecture to support it.

New paper: bit.ly/4bY6aL7

What's happening to make home prices so unaffordable for so many Americans?

"The overwhelming evidence points to persistent underproduction of housing as the most meaningful long-term driver." bit.ly/3PBfJYZ

In a recent study, RAND researchers asked AI chatbots a series of questions about suicide.

How did the chatbots respond (or not)?

Find out in a new episode of Policy Minded: bit.ly/4spcAtO

"The war has already succeeded in setting the Iranian threat back, and the United States retains multiple pathways forward. The real question is how much more risk should Washington accept—and over what time frame." bit.ly/4s9hM44
"My view is that [HUMINT] will have to have a human element—a real, essential human element—for the foreseeable future." defenseone.com/technology/20…
In a new episode of Policy Minded, RAND's Ryan McBain discusses the growing trend of young people using chatbots for mental health support: bit.ly/3PkRUV6

California is the "poster child" for letting housing affordability get out of hand, says RAND's Jason Ward.

"If you can address the problems in California, you're going to be able to address those same problems more easily almost anywhere else." bit.ly/4sEaI0b

"The idea of a sustained presence on the moon is orders of magnitude more complicated than just sending somebody to the moon," RAND's Bruce McClintock says ahead of the Artemis II mission. csmonitor.com/USA/Society/20…
New survey data: Educator resignations and retirements are approaching prepandemic levels. bit.ly/4rOuLYz

The Artemis program "is huge, it is historic," says RAND's Jan Osburg.

"But it's also important that it is not a flags-and-footprint thing anymore." csmonitor.com/USA/Society/20…

Between May and December 2025, the percentage of middle school, high school, and college students using AI for homework rose from 48% to 62%.

New survey results: bit.ly/4uAuYRE

New report identifies 3 objectives that strategic cooperation on AI could advance:

➡️ improving understanding of AI capabilities and risks

➡️ promoting reliable AI development while managing proliferation

➡️ preparing to mitigate and respond to harms

bit.ly/4rqcqRq
